source.title: Solutions of spinorial Yamabe-type problems on S^m: perturbations and applications

accepted.question_text: For a function f from the 2-sphere S^2 to the real numbers R, what conditions on f guarantee that there exists an isometric immersion Pi:S^2 -> R^3 whose mean curvature is f?

evidence.quote: what conditions on f guarantee the existence of an isometric immersion Pi : S2 -> R3 realizing f as its mean curvature?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a function f:S^2 -> R is the mean curvature function of an isometric immersion Pi:S^2 -> R^3. Can there exist another isometric immersion Pi_hat:S^2 -> R^3 that is not congruent to Pi but has the same mean curvature function f; if such another immersion exists, what can be said about the pull-back metrics Pi^*g_R3 and Pi_hat^*g_R3?
accepted.context_brief: Noncongruent isometric immersions with shared mean curvature

evidence.quote: Is it possible that there exists another isometric immersion bPi : S2 -> R3, not congruent with Pi, but also realizing f as its mean curvature?

needs_review.question_text_raw: It would be very interesting whether analogous results hold for dimension 3.

evidence.quote: It would be very interesting whether analogous results hold for dimension 3.
